text:
mariam-support: FYI customer on Private/VPC (CorpX) running the on-prem connector in no-internet mode is seeing intermittent failures to Redwood hosted endpoints. They get TLS errors and 502/timeout on generation requests.

mariam-support: Root log snippets they pasted: 
```
2026-03-12T14:22:11Z error request_id=abc123 tls: certificate signed by unknown authority
2026-03-12T14:22:11Z warn request_id=abc123 upstream: connect: permission denied
```

mariam-support: They say tokens look valid (auth OK), but generate endpoints return 502 or the connector times out. Happened after their corp proxy was upgraded to an inspection appliance.

olivia-support-sme: Can you get a failing request_id and the connector debug log with `REDWOOD_DEBUG=1`? Also ask if their proxy returns 407 vs. replaces certs (TLS MITM).

drew-eng-infra: Quick checklist to run against their gateway (share these with the customer):
1) `curl` test through proxy to control plane / api: 
```
# proxy with basic auth example
curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:3128 --proxy-user user:pass \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate
```
2) check for 407 responses (proxy auth) vs 502/521 (upstream): 
```
< HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required
< Proxy-Authenticate: NTLM
```
3) TLS chain check to upstream via the proxy (to detect CA replacement): 
```
# connect via tcp proxy (if allowed) or run from a host behind the proxy
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.com -showcerts
```

drew-eng-infra: Also verify DNS resolution from the connector host: `dig +short api.redwood-inference.com` and `getent hosts api.redwood-inference.com` — ensure it's not being rewritten to an internal IP by the proxy.

kevin-engruntime: If their proxy does TLS interception, the connector needs the corporate CA in the runtime trust store (OS / Java / glibc depending). If they prefer not to import root CA, they must allow passthrough for Redwood endpoints (SNI preserve) or use a proxy that supports CONNECT tunneling without MITM for 443.

mariam-support: Customer ran the curl test and attached verbose output. They have 502s and also occasional `tls: certificate signed by unknown authority` lines. They confirmed the proxy is doing inspection and the appliance injected its CA.

olivia-support-sme: Ask them to temporarily add the corporate root CA to the connector container's truststore and retry. Also confirm outbound allowlist IPs: we publish control-plane IP ranges at https://status.redwood-inference.com/egress-ips (ask them to allow these).

mariam-support: They tried adding CA -> still seeing intermittent 502s. They shared a tcpdump showing TLS handshake then RST from proxy after ~1s for larger responses.

drew-eng-infra: That looks like proxy has a size or time limit on tunneled streams. Two things to try:
- Enable `Connection: keep-alive`/chunked streaming test to see if proxy tears up long-lived connections.
- Route to dedicated control-plane region or try smaller payloads to reproduce.

deploy-bot: New support ticket created: #SUP-9182, linked.

kevin-engruntime: Repro command we use to simulate chunked streaming: 
```
# stream 1KB chunks repeatedly to see if proxy resets
python -c "import requests, time; s=requests.Session(); r=s.post('https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer x'}, json={'prompt':'hi','stream':true}, stream=True);\nfor chunk in r.iter_lines():\n  print(chunk)\n  time.sleep(0.1)\n" 
```

olivia-support-sme: If proxy resets when larger responses begin, their appliance may be doing response-body scanning and killing long-lived connections (common with naive inspection boxes). Ask for appliance vendor logs and whether there is an L7 idle/size policy.

mariam-support: Customer contacted appliance vendor; vendor says there is a default 30s per-stream limit and special handling for HTTP/2 multiplexed streams. They offered to bump timeouts and enable CONNECT passthrough for `api.redwood-inference.com`.

drew-eng-infra: Recommend these concrete remediation steps for the customer: 
- Allow passthrough (CONNECT) to api.redwood-inference.com and *.redwood-inference.com on 443.
- Whitelist our control-plane egress IPs (from the status page) in their firewall/egress allowlist.
- If MITM must remain, import corporate root CA into connector runtime truststore and increase proxy stream timeouts / body size thresholds.
- Ensure SNI is not rewritten by their proxy (we depend on SNI for routing). Verify with `openssl s_client -servername ...`.

mariam-support: Customer applied passthrough for `*.redwood-inference.com` and bumped timeouts. They report immediate improvement; no TLS errors and streaming now stable. They will schedule a longer soak test.

olivia-support-sme: Great — can we update our docs with a short checklist for on-prem/no-internet installs about proxy MITM caveats, required allowlist, and how to import CA? Opening an internal doc PR.

mariam-support: Closing the loop with customer, will keep ticket open until soak passes. :thumbsup:

kevin-engruntime: Filed follow-up GH issue to add a troubleshooting snippet (curl/opessl commands + example 407/502 differences) to the support KB.
